title: You’ll Never Walk Alone
description: Gerry Marsden’s band took this show tune from Rodgers and Hammerstein’s musical “Carousel” to No. 1 in 1963. Fans on the Kop, the home end at Liverpool FC’s Anfield stadium, adopted it as their anthem, and it is still sung before every home match.

title: Anyone Who Had a Heart
description: Cilla Black worked the cloakroom at the Cavern Club, the Mathew Street cellar where the Beatles played, before Brian Epstein signed her. Her version of this Burt Bacharach song went to No. 1 in 1964; a statue of her now stands outside the club.

title: Ferry Cross the Mersey
description: Gerry Marsden wrote this for the 1964 film of the same name, about the boats linking Liverpool and Birkenhead. The Mersey Ferries still leave from the Pier Head terminal, and the song plays on board as they cross the river.

title: Penny Lane
description: Paul McCartney’s picture of the street and bus terminus near where he and John Lennon grew up: the barber, the bank, the fireman and the “shelter in the middle of the roundabout,” which still stands at Smithdown Place by Penny Lane.

title: Strawberry Fields Forever
description: John Lennon grew up near Strawberry Field, a Salvation Army children’s home in Woolton, and played in its garden as a boy. The red gates are a pilgrimage spot, and the site now has a visitor centre about the home and the song.

title: Maggie Mae
description: A 40-second scrap of an old Liverpool sailors’ song on the Beatles’ “Let It Be,” about a woman who robbed a sailor “down Lime Street.” The street runs past Lime Street station, the city’s main railway terminus, and St George’s Hall.

title: Children of the Ghetto
description: Brothers Chris and Eddie Amoo of the Real Thing, Britain’s first Black chart-topping band, wrote this about their own district, Liverpool 8, or Toxteth. Granby Street was the heart of its Black community, one of the oldest in Britain.

title: Electricity
description: Andy McCluskey and Paul Humphreys, teenagers from Meols on the Wirral peninsula across the Mersey from Liverpool, formed OMD in 1978. This debut single, about wasted energy, came out on Manchester’s Factory Records in 1979.

title: Relax
place: Site of Eric’s club, Mathew Street
description: Singer Holly Johnson came out of the punk scene at Eric’s, the late-1970s club opposite the Cavern on Mathew Street. His band Frankie Goes to Hollywood’s debut was banned by BBC Radio 1 in 1984 and became one of Britain’s best-selling singles.

title: The Killing Moon
description: Ian McCulloch’s band Echo & the Bunnymen grew out of Liverpool’s post-punk scene; In May 1984 they led fans on “A Crystal Day” around the city, ending with a concert in St George’s Hall, the columned concert hall on Lime Street.

title: All Together Now
description: Peter Hooton’s band the Farm set the 1914 Christmas truce, when British and German soldiers stopped fighting, to Pachelbel’s Canon. A statue of the truce football match stands in St Luke’s, a church gutted in the 1941 Blitz and left roofless.

title: Dreaming of You
description: The Coral formed in Hoylake, a seaside town at the tip of the Wirral peninsula, as teenagers in the 1990s. This short, Merseybeat-tinged single from their 2002 debut album is the song most people know them by.

title: Let’s Dance to Joy Division
description: The Wombats met as students at LIPA, the performing arts school co-founded by Paul McCartney in his old school building on Mount Street. Matthew Murphy’s song is about dancing badly to the Manchester post-punk band Joy Division.
